script.title: Light: Exploring Mirrors and Lenses
script.subtitle: Master how light reflects and refracts to form perfect images.

steps.body: Light bounces off smooth surfaces like a ball hitting a wall.
Angle of Incidence (∠i) = Angle of Reflection (∠r).
Check if the image is Real (can be caught on screen) or Virtual (cannot).

script.example: Question: If a ray hits a plane mirror at 35° to the normal, find the angle of reflection. Answer: Since ∠i = ∠r, the angle of reflection is 35°.
script.ctaBody: Practice drawing ray diagrams for concave mirrors to ace your exams.
script.videoPrompt: A single laser beam hitting a curved mirror and splitting into multiple paths.

topics.heading: Reflection of Light
topics.explain: Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it hits a surface. It is like a tennis ball bouncing off a floor, where the direction changes based on the surface angle.
bullets: Regular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces.
Diffused reflection occurs on rough surfaces.
The incident ray, reflected ray, and normal all lie in the same plane.
topics.example: Smooth mirror = clear image; Rough wood = no clear image.
topics.visual: A beam of light hitting a polished silver plate and bouncing straight back.

topics.heading: Plane Mirrors
topics.explain: A plane mirror is a flat reflective surface. It creates images that look exactly like the object but are flipped left-to-right.
bullets: The image is always virtual and erect.
The image size is equal to the object size.
The distance of the object from the mirror equals the image distance.
topics.example: If you stand 2m from a mirror, your image is 2m behind it.
topics.visual: A student standing before a mirror with a 'left' hand appearing as a 'right' hand.

topics.heading: Spherical Mirrors
topics.explain: These mirrors have curved surfaces, like the inside or outside of a spoon. They are divided into Concave (curved inward) and Convex (bulged outward).
bullets: Concave mirrors can form real or virtual images.
Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images.
The Center of Curvature (C) is the center of the sphere.
topics.example: A dentist uses a concave mirror to see a larger image of a tooth.
topics.visual: A shiny spoon showing a tiny upright face on the back side.

topics.heading: Lenses: Refraction and Focus
topics.explain: Lenses use refraction, which is the bending of light as it passes through glass. Think of a straw looking broken in a glass of water.
bullets: Lenses form images based on their focal length.
topics.example: A magnifying glass uses a convex lens to enlarge text.
topics.visual: Light rays passing through a glass lens and meeting at a single point.

script.misconception: Students often think 'Real' means 'Actual'. In optics, 'Real' means the light rays actually meet to form an image on a screen.
script.examTip: Always use a sharp pencil and a ruler for ray diagrams; label the Incident Ray, Reflected Ray, and Normal clearly.
sources: NCERT Class 8 Science: Light: Mirrors and Lenses
